Swiss Timing Ltd is a Swiss sports-timekeeping company, part of the Swatch Group and
based in Corgémont, Switzerland. It develops timing, scoring, and display systems for
many sports, and its aquatics equipment is sold and displayed under the Omega brand at
major international meets. It is one of a small number of principal aquatic-timing
manufacturers, and the Omega line it produces is generally credited with the first
electronic swim-timing system using in-lane touchpads.[^history][^swatch][^wiki-timing]

Part of the Swiss Timing hardware documented in the
[equipment reference](../equipment/index.md) is
aquatic timing gear built around the company's Quantum console and OSB starting blocks.

## History

Swiss Timing was founded in 1972 in Biel, Switzerland, when the sports-timing
operations of two Swiss watch houses, Omega and Longines, were combined into a single
company. Both brands had timed sporting events for decades before then: Omega had served
as sole timekeeper of the 1932 Los Angeles Olympic Games, and Longines had a parallel
history in Olympic and equestrian timekeeping.[^history][^omega]

Swiss Timing became part of the Swatch Group through the 1983 merger, led by Nicolas G.
Hayek, of the watchmaking holdings ASUAG and SSIH into the company later renamed the
Swatch Group; the group retained Swiss Timing rather than dissolving it.[^swatch][^history]
In 1988 the Longines timing team and Omega sports timing were brought together under
Swiss Timing. The company is based in Corgémont, with additional offices in Leipzig,
Germany, and Liberec, Czech Republic, both from later acquisitions in those
countries.[^history]

Swiss Timing operates as the Swatch Group's timekeeping arm on behalf of the group's
watch brands. At the Olympic Games and other top-level events its equipment carries the
Omega name, under Omega's long-running role as official Olympic timekeeper, a role Omega
first held in 1932 and that runs under contract into the 2030s; Longines carries the
brand at other events.[^omega][^history]

## Products

Swiss Timing develops timing, scoring, and display systems across many sports, with a
dedicated aquatics line built around its Quantum console.[^history][^quantum]

- Aquatic timing, the Quantum Aquatics timing system, a primary and secondary console
  arrangement that collects finish signals from in-lane touchpads, receives the start
  pulse, runs the race clock, and drives the scoreboard, supplied with swimming
  software and cabling.[^quantum]
- Touchpads, the OMEGA OCP5 touchpad, which records a swimmer's finish at the wall; its
  contact strips close under about 2 to 3 kg of localized pressure and the surface is
  built to resist false impulses from waves and wash and to withstand hard water and
  pool chemicals.[^ocp5]
- Starting blocks, the OSB series of swimming starting blocks (the OSB11 and OSB14
  full blocks and the OSB12 platform), with an adjustable footrest, an anti-slip
  surface, and optional relay break detection (RBD) that judges relay exchanges from the
  block, plus the
  [OBL2 Pro backstroke ledge](../equipment/swimming/backstroke-start/swiss-timing.md)
  that gives backstrokers a fixed foothold at the start.[^osb11][^ocp5]
- Start systems, the StartTime electronic starting device, across the earlier acoustic
  StartTime II and III and the later StartTime IV and current StartTime V generations,
  whose e-gun (from the StartTime IV on) produces the start light and tone and drives the
  per-lane start audio.[^stconcept]
- Lane speakers, an in-block loudspeaker fitted inside the OSB blocks for fixed
  installations and mobile loudspeaker sets for portable cabling, both driven by the
  start device.[^stconcept]
- Scoreboards and displays, aquatic and multisport scoreboards and LED displays that
  show the race clock and results.[^quantum]
- Other sports, beyond aquatics Swiss Timing supplies timing, scoring, and results
  systems for a wide range of Olympic and international sports under the Omega and
  Longines brands.[^history]

Individual Swiss Timing aquatic products are catalogued in the
[equipment reference](../equipment/index.md): the
[StartTime II](../equipment/swimming/starter/starttime-ii.md),
[StartTime III](../equipment/swimming/starter/starttime-iii.md),
[StartTime IV](../equipment/swimming/starter/starttime-iv.md), and
[StartTime V](../equipment/swimming/starter/starttime-v.md) electronic starting
devices that start the race, the
[in-block and mobile lane speakers](../equipment/swimming/external-speaker/swiss-timing.md)
it drives under and around each block, and the
[OBL2 Pro backstroke ledge](../equipment/swimming/backstroke-start/swiss-timing.md)
that mounts on the OSB blocks. The Quantum console, OCP5 touchpads, and OSB
starting blocks are added as those pages are written.

## In swim timing

The first electronic swim-timing system using in-lane touchpads is generally credited to
Omega, in 1967, with contact pads designed to register a swimmer's touch rather than
incidental water movement. The 1964 Tokyo Olympic Games had already adopted a touch board
as the official timer for swimming, and the Munich 1972 report describes those earlier
boards as pneumatic rather than electronic.[^tokyo64][^munich72] Swiss Timing, which produces that Omega line today, is one of
a small number of major aquatic-timing manufacturers, alongside
[Colorado Time Systems](colorado-time-systems.md), [Daktronics](daktronics.md), and
[Seiko](seiko.md).[^wiki-timing] Its aquatics offering centers on the Quantum
console, which reads the OCP5 touchpads and backup buttons, receives the start pulse from
the StartTime device, runs the race clock, and drives the scoreboard.[^quantum][^stconcept]

## In competition

Swiss Timing equipment, under the Omega brand, is used at the Olympic Games and the World
Aquatics Championships and at other top-level international meets, where Omega serves as
official timekeeper.[^omega][^history] The company's aquatic systems are built to the
requirements of the international federation (World Aquatics, formerly FINA) that govern
timing and starting equipment at those competitions.[^quantum][^stconcept]
